Timothy Richard
TIM-uh-thee RICH-erd
proper noun
Welsh and biblical; Timothy from the Greek Timotheos, “honouring God,” the name of Paul’s beloved son in the faith, and Richard from the Germanic Ricohard, “strong ruler.” Borne by the Welsh Baptist missionary to China (1845–1919).

📖 Biblical Definition

Timothy Richard, a Welsh Baptist sent to China in 1870, laboured through decades of that land’s upheaval, and is chiefly honoured for his tireless relief of the poor and suffering, most notably in the great northern famine of the late 1870s, when he spent himself in feeding the starving and pressing the gospel upon a broken people. He believed the church must reach the whole man, and threw himself into the education, reform, and evangelizing of a vast heathen nation. His compassion in famine, his readiness to labour where death and misery reigned, and his zeal to make Christ known set a mark upon Protestant missions in China. Yet in his later years his esteem for the ancient religions of the East softened into a broad hope that the world’s faiths might somehow converge, a drift the church must name plainly as departure from the exclusive gospel of Christ, who alone is the way, the truth, and the life. The good in Richard—his mercy to the perishing, his industry, his love of a people not his own—we honour heartily; the erring in him—the blunting of the offence of the cross and the notion that other religions carry saving light—we must reject as error, for there is none other name under heaven whereby men must be saved. His life is thus both a summons to mercy and a warning that compassion untethered from the exclusivity of Christ loses the very gospel it means to give.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Welsh Baptist missionary to China, mighty in famine relief, later erring toward religious inclusivism.

expand to see more

A Welshman (1845–1919), Baptist Missionary Society worker in China from 1870.

A labourer of great compassion, spending himself in the northern famine relief of the late 1870s.

A promoter of education and reform among the Chinese as avenues for the gospel.

A man whose later years drifted toward a hope of convergence among the world religions—an error the church must name.

A mixed example: mercy to the perishing to be honoured, doctrinal drift to be rejected.

📖 Key Scripture

Act 4:12 — "Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved."

Joh 14:6 — "Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me."

Mat 25:35 — "For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:"

Gal 1:8 — "But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A genuine mixture: his famine mercy is honourable, but his later religious inclusivism is real error the church must name.

expand to see more

Unlike most figures in this dictionary, Richard presents a genuine mixture to be weighed. His labours in famine and his love for the Chinese poor are truly honourable, an image of Christ feeding the hungry and taking in the stranger. These we praise without reserve, as the fruit of a compassionate spirit spent for a perishing people.

But his later softening toward the ancient religions of China, and his hope that the world’s faiths might converge upon a common light, must be named plainly as error and not as breadth of vision. Scripture forecloses the notion: there is salvation in no other name, and Christ alone is the way to the Father. A gospel that dulls the offence of the cross to accommodate false religion is another gospel, and Paul pronounces it accursed. Richard’s drift is a warning that mercy must never be allowed to melt down the exclusivity of Christ.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Named to honour God, yet his later error dishonoured the one name in which alone is salvation.

expand to see more

Timothy — Greek Timotheos, “honouring God,” Paul’s own son in the faith.

Richard — Germanic Ricohard, “strong ruler.”

The root that must hold: the exclusive name of Act 4:12, given for salvation.

Christ the sole way, truth, and life of Joh 14:6—a root his later thought loosened.

The warning of Gal 1:8 against any other gospel, however compassionately dressed.

Usage

"Cited for heroic famine relief and compassion toward the suffering poor of China."

"Named also as a cautionary case where esteem for false religion eroded the exclusive gospel."

"Studied where the church weighs the boundary between mercy ministry and doctrinal fidelity."
